source: NPTEL Week 4 assessment, Jul–Oct 2026 run (accepted answers, reworded)

questions.question: Why has AI become so prominent in recent years?
options: AI no longer needs training data
More data, more computing power and better algorithms
AI can fully replace human intelligence
AI runs only in research labs

questions.question: What best separates AGI from narrow AI (ANI)?
options: Generalising knowledge across very different domains
questions.explanation: ANI excels at one task; AGI would transfer across domains.

questions.question: Correct relationship between AI, ML and deep learning:
questions.explanation: Deep learning is a subset of ML, which is a subset of AI.

questions.question: What fundamentally distinguishes generative from discriminative models?
options: Discriminative models learn the data distribution
Generative models learn how the data is generated

questions.question: Why is representation learning central to modern AI?
options: It removes the need for optimisation
It removes the need for labelled data
questions.explanation: Networks learn features instead of hand-engineering them.

questions.question: Which use case best shows the strength of generative AI?
options: Creating human-like text, images or audio
questions.explanation: Creating new content is what generative models add.

questions.question: A large language model is:
options: A neural model trained on massive text to learn language patterns
A supervised classifier with handcrafted features

questions.question: Why do transformers scale better than RNN-based models?
options: They rely on recurrence for memory

questions.question: A key reason transformer models are trending:
options: They keep improving with larger datasets and more compute
questions.explanation: Scaling laws: performance grows with data, parameters and compute.
